2. The plaintiff-petitioner filed Title suit No. 118 of 1996 in the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against the defendant-respondents praying a declaratory decree that the distribution and sup-ply of Daily Janakantha through its own employees/hawkers/agents on and from 8-5-96 in violation of the agency agreement dated 18-2-93 is illegal and for an injunction restraining the defendant-respondents from doing the same. On the date of filling of the suit, on i. e. on 6-6-96 the plaintiff-petitioner filed an application for temporary mandatory injunction for restraining the defendants from distributing Daily Janakantha through its employees/hawkers/agents in violation of the said agreement dated 18-2-93. On 6-6-98 the 'alai Court passed an order of ad-interim injunction restraining the defendant-respondents from doing so. The defendant-respondents thereafter obtained a Rule in the aforesaid civil revision from the High Court Division on 9-6-96 and operation of the order of ad-interim mandatory injunction was stayed. Upon hearing the parties the Rule was made absolute and hence the petition for leave to appeal by the plaintiff-petitioner. 

 3. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on finding that it was inequitable to ask one of the parties to an agreement to perform its obligation with-out asking the other party to do his obligation. By the impugned order of ad-interim mandatory injunction the suit has been practically tried out and the plaintiff-petitioner has been granted all the reliefs prayed for in the plaint, without noticing that the alleged loss sustained by the plaintiff does not come within the definition of irreparable loss and injury. Defendant-respondent No. 1 served notice dated 5-5-96 terminating the agency as per clause 6 of the agency agreement dated 18-3-96, according to which either party can terminate the agreement by serving two months notice on 'sufficient cause' which is at the discretion of the parties. In equity a court does not decree performance of an agreement in a case where parties are entitled to revoke or dis-solve the agreement. The impugned order was passed ex party in hot haste on the date of filing of the plaint and the trial Court failed to consider the matter in its proper perspective.
